content.text:
Late fees are now capped at the item's replacement cost. I haven't committed the change. All 61 tests pass, including the new one.

The fix is a `Math.min` in `assessLateFee` (`lib/fees/overdue-charges.js`). It was the only place a late fee is calculated, and `returnItem` calls it.

I added a test in `test/fees.test.js` for a return three months late. A laptop is charged 32000 cents, its replacement cost, instead of 500 cents a day for roughly 90 days. A book is charged 2200 cents.

I also recorded the reason for the cap in the repository's memory (Factloom).

The cap relies on `item.replacementCostCents`, which every item in the seed data and the tests has. If an item has no value for it, `Math.min` returns `NaN` and the fee would be wrong. I didn't add a fallback because I found no case where it's missing, but say if you want one.

The fix is a `Math.min` in `assessLateFee` (`lib/fees/overdue-charges.js`). It was the only place a late fee is calculated, and `returnItem` calls it.

I added a test in `test/fees.test.js` for a return three months late. A laptop is charged 32000 cents, its replacement cost, instead of 500 cents a day for roughly 90 days. A book is charged 2200 cents.

I also recorded the reason for the cap in the repository's memory (Factloom).

The cap relies on `item.replacementCostCents`, which every item in the seed data and the tests has. If an item has no value for it, `Math.min` returns `NaN` and the fee would be wrong. I didn't add a fallback because I found no case where it's missing, but say if you want one.
